## Surface aliases

UI vocabulary is not capability identity, but the mapping must be deterministic.
An alias creates no capability, no contract and no ownership.

| Surface word | Canonical LEGO | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `executions` | `execution` | Plural UI collection of execution records; the singular capability owns running and inspecting them. |
| `workflows` | `workflow` | Plural collection; singular capability owns the workflow entity. |
| `credentials` | `credentials` | Already plural in both vocabularies; recorded so the map is total rather than selective. |
| `projects` | `workspace` | The UI word is "project"; the architecture calls the domain workspace. This is a genuine rename, not a plural, which is exactly why it must be declared rather than guessed. |
| `node-types` | `node-registry` | UI speaks of node types; the domain owns the registry that resolves them. |

## Security capabilities and trust

Trust and capability are **separate axes**. A trust level does not imply a capability; capabilities are granted deliberately.

| Trust | Rank | Default grants | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `core` | 0 | `network`, `filesystem`, `subprocess`, `secrets`, `native`, `env` | First-party infrastructure. May run in-process. |
| `verified` | 1 | `network` | Reviewed/signed third party. In-process where its capabilities allow. |
| `community` | 2 | _none_ | Unreviewed community code. Restricted compatibility environment. |
| `untrusted` | 3 | _none_ | Unknown or hostile. Sandbox or worker only. |

Security capabilities: `network`, `filesystem`, `subprocess`, `secrets`, `native`, `env`.
